title: Locksmith at 2 a.m.
synopsis: You answer the after-hours line. The voice is small and far away.

nodes.text: An older woman locked out. She is on her front porch. It is freezing.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Care.

choices.text: Try to walk her through it
choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Wise.

nodes.text: She is wearing slippers. Her cat is, somehow, in the bushes.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Cat first” back. Heart shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Door first.” The story records the instinct as “Pragmatic” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Old. Cantankerous. Two minutes of patience.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Discipline.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Foolish—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: She turns on a kettle. Apologizes ten times. You wave her off.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honor.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Civil.

nodes.text: On the mantel, a young woman in uniform. She tells you about her daughter.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Listen.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Note the time, leave” back. Wise shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Dawn over the highway. You decide what kind of next month you want.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Bring more presence to it” back. Vow shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.

nodes.text: You become her once-a-month phone friend. You change a lightbulb for her sometimes. She bakes.
You go home, sleep four hours, eat pancakes. You feel, for an unrelated reason, hopeful.
